DETAILED ACTION
Notice of Pre-AIA  or AIA  Status
The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA .
Status of Claims
This Office Action is in response to the application filed on 8/17/2021.  Claims 1-13 are presently pending and are presented for examination.
Information Disclosure Statement
The information disclosure statement (IDS) submitted on 4/12/2021 is in compliance with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.97.  Accordingly, the information disclosure statement is being considered by the examiner.
Specification
The disclosure is objected to because of the following informalities:
[0071] The cell B1 is addressed as a priority and, if it is able to supply a sufficient current lmax,1> Is, it is the only one that is addressed.
It is unclear what is meant by “addressing” a cell.
[0074] The Applicant performed simulations with assemblies comprising a variable number of lithium-ion micro batteries such as the one shown above.
The specification does not sufficiently identify the lithium-ion micro batteries that are “shown above”
Appropriate correction is required.
Drawings
The drawings filed 04/12/2021 are objected to because the images and labels are unclear and illegible.
Specifically the printing or drawing method used by the Applicant combined with the small font size causes the images and drawing labels to appear “blurry” and illegible.
For example, the images in Figs. 8-10 appear “blurry” and the corresponding labels and lettering (Figs. 5,8-10 and 13-16 for example) also appearing “blurry”.
The Examiner recommends correcting all drawings in such a way that the figures and labels are clear and legible, and the quality of the figures are equivalent to the quality produced by a laser printer.
Corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment of the application. Any amended replacement drawing sheet should include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is being amended. The figure or figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as “amended.” If a drawing figure is to be canceled, the appropriate figure must be removed from the replacement sheet, and where necessary, the remaining figures must be renumbered and appropriate changes made to the brief description of the several views of the drawings for consistency. Additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show the renumbering of the remaining figures. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of an application must be labeled in the top margin as either “Replacement Sheet” or “New Sheet” pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). If the changes are not accepted by the examiner, the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action. The objection to the drawings will not be held in abeyance.
Examiners note on claim interpretation
In regards to claim language “all times t” and “at all times”, based on the specification (For ex. Fig. 8-11 and [0052]-[0055] and claim 1, i.e. “the first electrical energy storage or production cell until it is totally depleted”) supports that the current ends when the battery capacity is depleted. Therefore Examiner will interpret “at all times” as “continuously during the time period T”.
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 112
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112 (b), second paragraph:
The specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the applicant regards as his invention.
Claims 1-13 is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA ), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA  the applicant regards as the invention.
As to claim 1, which recites “said management circuit comprises means, in discharge mode, for addressing at least the electrical energy storage or production cell of rank 1 or the electrical energy storage or production cells according to their rank i and according to the following criteria” which is unclear..
It is unclear what it means to “address” an electrical energy storage or production cell.
As to claim 1, which recites “the electrical energy storage or production cell (B1) of rank 1 is addressed on its own” which is unclear.
It is unclear what it means to “address” an electrical energy storage or production cell.
It is also unclear what is meant or how an electrical energy storage or production cell is “addressed on its own”
As to claim 1, which recites “the electrical energy storage or production cell (B1) of rank 1 is addressed with additionally a number k of electrical energy storage or production cells (Bi) that are addressed successively according to their rank i, so as to supply the current Is at all times in discharge mode” which is unclear.
It is unclear what it means to “address” an electrical energy storage or production cell.
Additionally, claim language “at all times” includes that the current is supplied indefinitely.
However, the specification (For example Fig. 8-11 and [0052]-[0055] ) explains that the current ends when the battery capacity is depleted.
It is unclear what  is meant by the current is supplied “at all times”. Examiner will interpret “at all times” as “continuously during the time period T”
As to claim 2 , which recites “the management circuit for managing said electrical energy storage or production cells controlling each of said electrical energy storage or production cells (Bi) through hysteresis in all-or-nothing mode” which is unclear.
It is unclear what is meant by an “all-or-nothing mode”
As to claim 4 , which recites “the cell of rank 1 (B1) is activated on its own” which is unclear.
It is unclear what is meant by (B1) being activated “on its own”
As to claim 8 , which recites “wherein the management circuit comprises means, in recharge mode, corresponding to a negative output current -Is, for placing all of the cells in parallel” which is unclear.
Specifically, it is unclear how is the means corresponding to a negative output current is for placing all of the cells in parallel.
As to claim 9 , which recites “wherein the management circuit comprises means, in recharge mode, corresponding to a negative output current -Is, for addressing the cells of high rank as a priority” which is unclear.
It is unclear what it means to “address” an electrical energy storage or production cell.
Examiner will interpret to “address” an electrical energy storage or production cell as to “discharge/charge” an electrical energy storage or production cell.
Claims 2-13 is/are included in this rejection due to their dependence on claim 1.

Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.

Conclusion and Related Art
The prior art made of record and not relied upon is considered pertinent to applicant's disclosure.
Sharma et al (US 20220294036)  is cited for discharging power from battery packs to a grid or charging power to battery packs based on the power rate of each battery pack.
Tikhonski (US 20220037910) is cited for monitoring an output voltage delivered to the distribution bus, wherein the output voltage results from a delivery of current to the distribution bus by a first power source; and delivering current from a second power source to the distribution bus via a DC-DC converter when the monitored output voltage decreases to a level equivalent to a voltage regulation setpoint of the DC-DC converter. However Tikhonski’s effective filing date for this feature is after the filing date of the instant application.
